facts: The paper 'Irrational exuberance and neural crash warning signals during endogenous experimental market bubbles' was authored by Alec Smith, Terry Lohrenz, Justin King, P. Read Montague, and Colin F. Camerer.
The study was published on 2014-07-07 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS).
The study investigated the behavioral and neural underpinnings of group decision-making during asset price bubbles.
The experimental markets were determined by 11–23 subjects, with 2–3 subjects simultaneously scanned using functional MRI (fMRI).
Activity in the nucleus accumbens (NAcc) tracked the price bubble and predicted future price changes.
Traders who bought more aggressively based on nucleus accumbens (NAcc) signals earned less.
High-earning traders exhibited early warning signals in the anterior insular cortex prior to peak prices and sold coincidentally with that signal, precipitating the market crash.
The findings suggest these experiments can aid in understanding situations where human groups miscompute the value of actions or events.
